title: identity.oidc_client.revoked payload
description: The `data` payload of the `identity.oidc_client.revoked` event: a registration stopped being honoured. The registration's row id is the envelope's `subject` and is not repeated in `data`; `client_id` below is the string the relying party presents, and the two are different values. The row is KEPT rather than deleted — an audit of which credentials existed is worth more than a tidier table, and a DELETE would also lose the record of which redirect URIs a compromised product held — so `revoked_at` on the row is what makes the difference readable afterwards. The transaction that appends this event ALSO bulk-revokes every access token issued against the registration, which is the reason a subscriber may treat this type as "stop trusting this client AND everything already issued under it": a token is a signed JWT, so it is verifiable by anybody holding the published key set until its `exp` arrives, and revoking the registration on its own leaves a window in which a credential nobody has revoked is still good. There is no `revoke_reason`: the row carries it, because a reason is operator-facing context typed by a human at a call site and a field whose values vary per operator is a field every consumer learns to ignore. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

client_id.description: The `client_id` the registration was issued, and the value to strike from a product's configuration. Not the envelope's `subject`, which is the registration's row id — see the description above. Carrying it here is what lets a consumer that only ever saw the string act on the revocation without a lookup it may not be able to make.

account_id.description: The account the registration belonged to. Read out of the row before the update rather than taken from the request, so a revocation of something that is not there says so instead of announcing nothing.

revoked_by.description: The user who revoked it. The `actor`, and never null: the row's revocation columns are set together or not at all by a CHECK, so a row revoked with no `revoked_by` could not be attributed and a row revoked twice would be a second revocation of something already dead.
